status: REAL measured results from a rebuilt pipeline -- not the thesis's original claims. See chapter7_reference_numbers.md for the original claims to compare against.
model_version: v3: combined UDP+SYN dataset (180 files) + real feature engineering (syn_noack_ratio, ack_ratio added) + real leakage-safe hyperparameter search (max_depth=9, learning_rate=0.2). Supersedes v2 (combined dataset, original 8 features, depth=6, 83.46% accuracy) and v1 (40-file UDP-only, 88.2% accuracy).

dataset.source: CIC-DDoS2019 official UNB download, PCAPs/01-12: 111 files spread evenly across chunk 1 (_0.._0249, real sustained UDP flood throughout) + all 69 files of chunk 4 (_0750.._0818, UDP continuation with a real SYN flood emerging in the tail files -- 180 files total).
dataset.capture_date_caveat: Raw pcap timestamps read 2018-12-01, not the commonly-cited 2019 dates -- flagged as an unresolved data-quality anomaly, not corrected or assumed away.
dataset.attack_ground_truth: 172.16.0.5 confirmed via forensic packet inspection as the sole real attacker. Each (src_ip, 0.5s window) is labeled with a real attack TYPE from actual packet content: 'udp' if UDP-dominant, 'syn' if dominated by TCP SYN-without-ACK packets, 'benign' otherwise.

feature_set.note: syn_noack_ratio and ack_ratio added after a real evaluation (evaluation_output/feature_engineering_results.json) found the single generic tcp_flags feature (SYN fraction) conflated real handshake SYNs with attack SYN-flood packets. Both are computed over the SAME 0.5s window as the other 8 features -- no detection-latency cost, unlike widening the window (also real-tested; see window_size_research below).

real_ablation.label: C: B's 10 features + tuned depth=9 (real CV-search best from earlier)

hyperparameters.note: max_depth and learning_rate retuned from the thesis's original (6, 0.1) via a real leakage-safe 3-fold CV search (train-split only; scripts/tune_model_search.py) -- the held-out test set was touched exactly once for the final reported number.

split_method_note: NOT a single global temporal split. Because real SYN data is concentrated in the last handful of files in the whole capture, a naive 'first 80% of capture-time = train' split would put almost all SYN examples in test and none in training. Instead each attack type (benign/udp/syn) is split 80/20 by time WITHIN that type, then combined.

values.stage: Feature vector assembly (real Redis-backed sliding window)
P4Runtime rule installation (real Thrift RPC to live simple_switch)

latency_breakdown.STALE_WARNING: Measured against the PRIOR 8-feature/depth=6 model, not yet re-run against the current 10-feature/depth=9 production model. Not expected to change materially (2 extra ratio features and 3 extra tree-depth levels are a negligible addition to a single XGBoost predict() call), but not re-measured for real -- re-run scripts/run_latency_trials.sh if this needs to be reported as current rather than representative.

values.note: Real ablation studies re-run on the real pipeline. Only 4 of the original thesis's 6 are included -- the other 2 either aren't feasible on this software-switch (BMv2) setup or weren't run for real; see 'not_run' below rather than any fabricated placeholder numbers. feature_dimensionality, tree_depth, and register_granularity were re-run a second time (this version) on the expanded 180-file combined UDP+SYN dataset (83,457 window-rows) using the same per-type temporal 80/20 split as the main training run -- the earlier version of this file used the older 40-file UDP-only dataset. bloom_deduplication and threshold_T are unchanged: both are live single-replay switch measurements independent of the training dataset/model, so they were not re-run.

feature_dimensionality.method: Retrained real XGBoost on the same real per-type temporal 80/20 split (controller/ml/train_model.py's per_type_temporal_split, combined UDP+SYN 83,457-row dataset), varying which of the 8 real features are included. Weighted-avg F1 and FPR from real confusion matrices; inference time is a real single-row microbenchmark (100 repeats, mean).

results.feature_set: Basic (4 features: pkt_rate, byte_rate, port_div, tcp_flags)

feature_dimensionality.finding: F1 decreases monotonically with fewer features (0.827->0.740->0.711), same direction as the thesis's claim (0.974->0.932->0.891) but smaller real magnitude, and starting from a much lower real baseline. FPR drops sharply going from 8 to 4 features (7.32%->0.82%) then ticks up slightly at 2 features (0.92%) -- consistent with a model that becomes more conservative (fewer false alarms, but also less recall) as features are removed, not a smooth thesis-style progression.

tree_depth.method: Retrained real XGBoost at max_depth in {3,6,9,12}, same real per-type temporal split (combined UDP+SYN dataset). Same single-row microbenchmark methodology for inference time.
tree_depth.finding: Unlike the earlier 40-file UDP-only run (where F1 plateaued almost immediately past depth 6), on this harder combined UDP+SYN task F1 keeps rising all the way to depth 12 (0.712->0.827->0.840->0.846), driven mostly by recall climbing (0.132->0.552->0.620->0.634) as the model gets more capacity to separate the much rarer, harder-to-learn SYN class from benign traffic. Inference-time numbers remain noisy millisecond-scale microbenchmarks with no clean depth->latency relationship, same as before -- flagged as measurement noise, not reported as a real trend.

register_granularity.method: Real distinct source IPs (536, up from 355 in the earlier 40-file sample now that the dataset spans 180 files) from the real extracted dataset, hashed via the same crc16-via-crc32 approximation baseline_reimpl/common.py already uses and flags -- not bit-identical to BMv2's real CRC16 hash extern.
register_granularity.finding: At P4-XGBoost's actual chosen width (1024), real collision rate is 43.10% -- still dramatically higher than the thesis's claimed 3.8%, and higher than the earlier 40-file run's 30.99% because the expanded dataset now has 536 distinct source IPs sharing the same 1024 slots (a modest real sample either way, not the larger population the thesis's number implied).

bloom_deduplication.method: Real simple_switch log inspection: replayed the real 150-packet attacker trigger slice once, counted (a) how many packets crossed the CMS threshold (would each attempt a digest without dedup) vs (b) how many bloom_reg writes actually occurred (real digest-eligible events, i.e. with dedup as currently implemented).
bloom_deduplication.finding: Real ~50x reduction in digest volume from dedup on just this small 150-packet slice. Over the full real ~15.78M-packet attacker flow in the 40-file sample, the reduction would be dramatically larger -- dedup keeps digest volume to 1 per source IP for the switch's lifetime regardless of how many packets keep crossing the threshold. Not re-run against the expanded 180-file dataset: this is a live single-replay switch measurement independent of the training dataset/model, using the same fixed attacker_trigger_slice.pcap as before.

threshold_T.method: Real inter-arrival timestamps from the real 150-packet attacker trigger slice -- how long (real elapsed time) it actually took this real attacker to send T packets.
threshold_T.finding: MAJOR real divergence, not a minor detail: at the thesis's own chosen T=100, this real attacker's actual packet rate takes ~23.75 SECONDS of real elapsed time to cross the threshold -- nowhere close to the thesis's implied ~28ms total end-to-end latency budget. The thesis's 28ms figure apparently only ever measured the controller-side pipeline after a digest already existed, not the real data-plane accumulation time needed to generate one in the first place. This attacker sends a sustained moderate-rate flood, not a rapid burst -- see stage #7's forensic finding. Not re-run against the expanded 180-file dataset: this is a live single-replay switch measurement independent of the training dataset/model, using the same fixed attacker_trigger_slice.pcap as before.

not_run.digest_payload_size: Requires comparing against real Tofino ASIC line-rate throughput (>5,000 alerts/sec claim in the thesis) -- BMv2 is a software reference switch and cannot faithfully reproduce Tofino performance, same reasoning baseline_reimpl/README.md already applies to excluding throughput/latency baseline comparisons. Dropped rather than faked with a software-switch number presented as if it were hardware-comparable.

ablations.STALE_WARNING: feature_dimensionality, tree_depth, and register_granularity sections were measured against the PRIOR 8-feature/depth-sweep-from-6 model/dataset state, before the syn_noack_ratio/ack_ratio features were added. Not yet re-run against the new 10-feature production feature set.

window_size_research.summary: A real window-size sweep (0.1s-4.0s, scripts/window_sweep.py) found accuracy rises substantially with window size (78.5% at 0.1s to 94.2% at 4.0s), but at a real, disclosed detection-latency cost -- a bigger window means the feature vector can't be finalized until that much real time has passed. The production model keeps the original 0.5s window and instead improved accuracy via feature engineering + hyperparameter tuning (83.46%->86.22%), which has NO latency cost.

full_flow_original.note: Jaqen-lite, POSEIDON-lite, and FlowLens-lite as originally evaluated: on COMPLETE real flows (median ~3.0s for a real UDP-attack flow, ~5.0s for a real SYN-attack flow, tail into the thousands of seconds), NOT the same 0.5s window P4-XGBoost decides on. Kept here for transparency/comparison, but see 'windowed_apples_to_apples' below for the fair comparison.

windowed_apples_to_apples.note: All three baselines re-evaluated at the SAME real 0.5s fixed window P4-XGBoost uses, for a genuinely matched real-time operating point. Jaqen-lite and POSEIDON-lite are threshold rules (not trained), so both an 'as-originally-configured' pass and a 'retuned' pass (real leakage-safe grid search on the TRAINING split only, applied once to test) are reported -- retuning matters here because their real thresholds (SYN_THRESH=20 etc.) were implicitly calibrated for real per-complete-flow counts, not 0.5s-window counts, and reporting them unchanged would unfairly deflate those baselines. FlowLens-lite is offline functional re-creation (not a live BMv2 measurement), consistent with the other two.

baseline_comparison.finding: At a genuinely matched 0.5s real-time operating point, P4-XGBoost (86.22% accuracy, 0.711 attack F1) outperforms all three baselines, including after fairly retuning Jaqen-lite and POSEIDON-lite's thresholds for that window (Jaqen-lite retuned: 72.25% accuracy / 0.104 attack F1; POSEIDON-lite retuned: 38.46% / 0.210; FlowLens-lite windowed: 79.40% / 0.358). This is the honest, apples-to-apples headline result -- not the full-flow numbers, where FlowLens-lite's 99.2% accuracy reflects a fundamentally slower real operating point (waiting for an entire flow), not a stronger detector at matched speed.
